When a complaint was made against the contractor Haridas Bhagwandas to the British Government Officer, he did not pay any attention.

slides.text: In Chhattisgarh , the national level movements were in effect and they were led by the freedom fighters of the state, they started with the revolution of 1857 which continued till the attainment of independence of India. T here was a substantial revolution against the British Empire, as a result of this revolution in Chhattisgarh, there were rebellions in many areas against the exploitative governance of the British. Gandhian Independence Movement i n Chhattisgarh Third Era o f the Final Solution to the Freedom Mahatma Gandhi had taken a stand - in Chhattisgarh to find out that the "˜ Non-Cooperation Movement ' which is the Congress was still contemplating how to do, but in a small village in Chhattisgarh h ad already started this movement by Babu Chhotelal Shrivastava , which became the pave way of non-cooperation movements in subsequent movements.

The manner in which the British Indian forces presented a model of coercion and inhumanity to obey orders gave further impetus to the struggle and the people of Chhattisgarh set an example of indomitable struggle and discipline. The Kandel Canal Satyagraha was an independent struggle, but we remember it only in the context of Gandhi ' s first arrival in Chhattisgarh.

slides.text: In these places, the British administration had presented such a horrific scene of repression that in 1931 the Mahakoshal Congress Committee had to ask the Raipur District Congress Committee to investigate the matter. Thakur Pyarelal Singh was then a minister of the Mahakoshal Congress Committee. Under his leadership, Pandit Bhagwatiprasad Mishra, Yeti Yatanlal , and Maulana Abdul Rauf Khan visited some of the affected villages and recorded the statements of the victims.

slides.text: The investigation team had only 4 - 5 days of deferment. Tha kur Pyarelal Singh has admitted that he did not get enough time to investigate and make a report. But from the statements of more than a hundred victims, it can only be estimated how m any atrocities were committed in Mahasamund Tehsil.

slides.text: If such atrocities had been committed in the villages near Raipur, there would have been a huge reaction, no doubt. Headless villagers faced the British administration with great courage. People were beaten up, heavy fines were levied, and cash and jewelry looted from people ' s homes, rice, ghee, vegetables, goats, poultry, cow , and bulls were also taken away.
